extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, and readers interested in publication ethics and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: Identifying and responding to duplicate or substantially overlapping submissions/publications in mathematical journals, including grounds for retraction and corrective actions. The page reports a specific case and quotes journal/retraction language and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / exclusive submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Editors and publishers of the journal, Taylor & Francis, note that we received, peer-reviewed, accepted and published the article on the basis that the authors are presenting original results and are not intending to publish them in any other journal."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals expect submitted work to be original and not under consideration elsewhere; publishing is done on the basis that authors are not intending to publish the same results in another journal. Violation of this principle can trigger editorial action (withdrawal/retraction) and may reflect a contract breach between author and publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial overlap / duplicate publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice states the article "has substantial overlap with an article by Jin Li, Jianlin Luo, and Zaihong Wang" (i.e., two papers share large amounts of text/results/abstract content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When two published articles overlap substantially, journals treat the case as duplicate publication. Overlap between two papers that present the same results or text is a primary ground for duplication retractions; the post illustrates this by showing nearly identical abstracts and noting the timing of submissions/publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of publication ethics warrants retraction (per COPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: "This is a violation of publication ethics which, in accordance with the Committee on Publication Ethics guidelines, warrants a retraction of the article and a notice to this effect to be published in the journal."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may rely on COPE guidelines to decide that certain ethical breaches (such as duplicate publication) require formal retraction and an accompanying published notice. The guidance implies using recognized ethics frameworks (e.g., COPE) to determine corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial/publisher responsibility to investigate and notify
rubrics_metrics.description: The article was retracted after it "was brought to the attention of the editorial and publishing staff that this article has substantial overlap" and the Editor-in-Chief issued the retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and publishing staff are expected to investigate reports of overlap or ethical concerns and, if warranted, issue retractions/notices. Procedurally, discovery by editorial staff can trigger formal investigation and corrective publication actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous or near-simultaneous submissions are problematic
rubrics_metrics.description: Both journals received the papers within a few months of each other and published them in quick succession; a commenter notes "This is an inevitable outcome of simultaneous submission."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting the same or substantially similar manuscripts to multiple journals at once (or very close in time) can lead to duplicated publication and retractions. The post implicitly treats near-simultaneous submissions as an anti-pattern that can 'dupe' editors and violate journal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections/errata for errors in published work
rubrics_metrics.description: An erratum was published for another Li paper in 2014: it "fixes errors in 'Existence and uniqueness of anti-periodic solutions for prescribed mean curvature Rayleigh equations'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When genuine errors are identified in published work, journals issue errata/corrections to fix the record. This is a distinct corrective mechanism from retraction and is appropriate when problems are errors rather than ethical breaches that invalidate originality claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between scientific validity and publication ethics in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: A commenter observes: "the validity of the results can be established (and hopefully were established in peer review) without the need to trust the author. This is unlike data-sciences where one could falsify or make up data."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In mathematics, the community can often verify results independently, so ethical breaches around duplication affect the publication record and authorship/attribution rather than necessarily invalidating the mathematical results themselves. This can influence debates about whether duplication should lead to one or both retractions versus preserving a single valid record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notice as standard remedy for duplication cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The post describes the retraction notices as "pretty standard as far as duplication retractions go" and reproduces standard retraction wording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing a formal retraction notice explaining the reason (e.g., substantial overlap, breach of exclusive-submission policy) is the customary remedy for duplicate publication. The notice typically names the editor/publisher and cites the ethical grounds and relevant policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential contractual/administrative consequences for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: A commenter notes editors "might well have a contract issue with Li," and the Taylor & Francis notice implies contractual expectations about originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond correction of the literature, duplicate submission/publication can create contractual disputes between authors and publishers and may carry administrative consequences (e.g., sanctions by institutions or publishers) though the page gives no detailed procedure for these outcomes.
